nutshell: Facial landmark localization for niche domains (animals, art portraits, caricatures, illusory 'pareidolia' faces) is hard because labeled datasets are tiny and use inconsistent landmark definitions across domains. MDMD introduces a ViT encoder plus a transformer decoder built around 12 shared 'Facial Landmark Semantic Group' (FLSG) tokens, letting one model train concurrently across datasets with different landmark counts/definitions by routing decoder outputs to per-dataset regression heads.
contributions: Facial Landmark Semantic Group (FLSG): a fixed set of 12 learned embedding tokens representing abstract facial regions (eyes, nose, etc.) shared across all domains/definitions, letting heterogeneous landmark schemas be unified in one decoder rather than needing per-dataset architecture.

A definition-agnostic transformer decoder where FLSG tokens cross-attend to ViT image features and self-attend to each other, then route to per-dataset/definition MLP heads that regress both landmark means and Cholesky-factorized covariance via a Laplacian log-likelihood loss.

Demonstrates large gains on small/novel-domain datasets (a 100-image macaque subset of AnimWeb, ArtFace portraits, CariFace caricatures, and a new 150-image pareidolia dataset the authors contribute) when co-trained with a larger source dataset (300W or LaPa), plus competitive-to-SOTA results on the standard COFW and WFLW benchmarks.
deficiencies: The paper's own ablation (Table 5) shows FLSG actually underperforms a simpler explicit-individual-landmark-token baseline in the single-dataset case (4.82 vs. 4.73 NME on COFW alone) - the central architectural idea only pays off once a co-training partner dataset is added, which the paper acknowledges but doesn't resolve.

The small-domain 'SOTA' comparisons are explicitly not apples-to-apples: the paper trains CariFace on 148 images vs. Zhang et al.'s 6,420, and AnimWeb on a single macaque subset vs. Khan et al.'s full 21,900-image multi-species set, then still frames results as competitive/SOTA despite noting these are only 'ballpark' comparisons.

On WFLW (Table 2), two concurrent works (FaRL, SH-FAN) beat MDMD w/LaPa on overall NME/FR/AUC (e.g. SH-FAN 3.72 vs. MDMD's 3.97 NME) - the 'outperforms all previous SOTA aside from two concurrent works' framing carries a fairly load-bearing caveat.

Novel-domain test sets are extremely small (33 test monkey faces, 3 held-out images per artist across 16 artists for ArtFace) with no reported variance across seeds/runs, so the reported NME/FR/AUC swings rest on very few examples.
notable: The paper includes a dedicated qualitative failure-case figure (Fig. 5: extreme pose/occlusion, an extremely deformed caricature) rather than only showcasing successes - a good-faith practice not every paper in this batch bothers with. Also: references [19] and [20] are the same paper (Jin et al., 'Separable batch normalization for robust facial landmark localization') cited twice under different numbers - the same duplicate-citation pattern seen elsewhere in this literature review.
